scope.flow: StakingManager withdrawal lifecycle: queueWithdrawal adds an L1 UserWithdrawal operation to _pendingWithdrawals; MANAGER_ROLE cancelWithdrawal refunds kHYPE and records _cancelledWithdrawalAmount; OPERATOR_ROLE processL1Operations later executes queued L1 operations
scope.environment: StakingManager.sol L2 contract with L1 queue processing via l1Write.sendTokenDelegate/sendCWithdrawal

statements.text: A user has locked kHYPE via queueWithdrawal, creating a UserWithdrawal operation in the _pendingWithdrawals queue and a record in _withdrawalRequests.
A role holding MANAGER_ROLE calls cancelWithdrawal on the user's withdrawal request.
A role holding OPERATOR_ROLE calls processL1Operations, which processes operations in the _pendingWithdrawals queue.
cancelWithdrawal deletes the _withdrawalRequests record, returns locked kHYPE including fees to the user, and accumulates the cancelled HYPE amount after fees into _cancelledWithdrawalAmount.
processL1Operations sequentially calls l1Write.sendTokenDelegate(..., true) and l1Write.sendCWithdrawal(...) for each queued operation to complete undelegation and fund transfer on L1.
cancelWithdrawal does not remove the corresponding L1 withdrawal operation from the _pendingWithdrawals queue.
When a withdrawal request is cancelled, the corresponding L1 withdrawal operation must be removed from the _pendingWithdrawals queue so it is not later executed.
A cancelled withdrawal must not be processed twice: once by returning kHYPE to the user and once by withdrawing HYPE from L1.
The value balance between HYPE and kHYPE must be preserved, with protocol HYPE holdings corresponding to total kHYPE supply.

Although the withdrawal request on L2 has been cancelled and the user has retrieved their kHYPE, the existing L1 withdrawal operation in the queue will still be executed as long as the OPERATOR_ROLE calls processL1Operations, so HYPE will be undelegated from the L1 validator and transferred as usual.
The same cancelled withdrawal is effectively processed twice, once to return the kHYPE to the user and once to withdraw the HYPE from L1, breaking the value balance between HYPE and kHYPE.
The relationship between the protocol's HYPE holdings and the total kHYPE supply becomes confused, causing the exchange rate calculated by the StakingAccountant to deviate significantly from reality.

The state of confusion and value imbalance could be exploited by attackers familiar with the protocol mechanism, for example by manipulating the timing of cancellations and processing combined with a distorted exchange rate to find arbitrage opportunities or extract additional value from the protocol.
